text:
Maya: Hey support — customer on Private VPC started failing SSO after their IdP rotated certs around 10:00 UTC. Errors in our auth logs: "AssertionConsumerService URL mismatch" and "Signature verification failed". Ticket SUP-4021. Anyone seen this pattern?
Samuel: Thanks — can you paste their IdP metadata XML (or link) and confirm the ACS URL configured on our side plus when they published metadata?
Maya: Their metadata is at https://idp.customer.example.com/metadata. It shows two <KeyDescriptor use='signing'> entries (old and new). They say rotation happened 2026-03-16T10:00Z. Our ACS configured: https://app.customer.example.com/saml/acs (no trailing slash).
Eli: Quick checks — trailing slash/canonicalization of entityID or ACS can cause AssertionConsumerService URL mismatch. Also if metadata has duplicate KeyDescriptor entries ordering changed, some responses might be signed with a key we don't trust yet.
Maya: I ran a quick extract: `curl -sS https://idp.customer.example.com/metadata | xmllint --xpath 'string(//EntityDescriptor/@entityID)' -` -> `https://idp.customer.example.com/` (note trailing slash). Our SP entityID: `https://app.customer.example.com/saml` (no slash).
Ingrid: Trailing slash could cause audience/recipient mismatch but not a signature failure. For signatures, we need to check which KeyInfo was used in the SAMLResponse. Can you paste the base64 SAMLResponse decoded (redact PII) or at least the Signature KeyInfo fingerprint?
Maya: Here's the redacted snippet from the SAMLResponse (extracted from debug logs):
```
<signedAssertion ...>
  <Signature>
    <KeyInfo>
      <X509Data><X509Certificate>MIIC...BASE64...==</X509Certificate></X509Data>
    </KeyInfo>
  </Signature>
  <SubjectConfirmationData Recipient="https://app.customer.example.com/saml/acs"/>
</signedAssertion>
```
Note Recipient includes a trailing slash while our configured ACS does not. Also the cert fingerprint in the logs shows sha1=AB:12:34:56:78:9C:... which does not match the cert currently in our idp_trusted_certs store for this customer.
Eli: Looks like two issues overlapped: 1) metadata entityID/ACS canonicalization (trailing slash) causing recipient/audience mismatch; 2) IdP rotation left some responses signed by an older cert or by a cert we haven't hot-loaded because metadata contained duplicate KeyDescriptor entries and our cached Key list did not include the signing key used. I've seen this when IdP publishes both keys but changes ordering and our parsing logic only picked the first one.
Maya: Customer can't republish a cleaned metadata immediately. Is there a safe hotfix we can apply on our side to accept the new fingerprint? This is a production-facing outage for them.
Samuel: Hotfix path (private/dedicated):
1) fetch metadata and extract X509 cert: `curl -s https://idp.customer.example.com/metadata | xmllint --xpath 'string(//KeyDescriptor[@use=\'signing\']/KeyInfo/X509Data/X509Certificate)' -`
2) compute fingerprint: `echo -n 'MIIC...==' | base64 -d | openssl x509 -noout -fingerprint -sha1`
3) add fingerprint to customer entry in admin UI: Settings -> SSO -> Advanced -> Trusted certs (we support hot-reload for private installs).
4) restart auth proxy on their nodes: `systemctl restart redwood-auth-proxy` (rolling, one node at a time) OR trigger a rolling deploy via Console for hosted/dedicated.
I'll coordinate the restart if you don't have permissions.
Maya: Extracted sha1 fingerprint: AB:12:34:56:78:9C:DE:F0:11:22:33:44:55:66:77:88:99:AA:BB:CC (redacted). I can add the cert in the admin UI but don't have permission to restart the agent inside their VPC. @oncall-chris can you do a rolling restart for customer-id=789?
oncall-chris: I can take that. Confirming window 10:45-10:50 UTC for a rolling restart. I'll tail auth logs and watch for 502s. Doing one node at a time so traffic stays healthy. :thumbsup:
support-bot: ACTION — Escalation created: SUP-4021 -> ENG-ONCALL. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SUP-4021. Priority: P2. Steps & artifacts attached.
Maya: Restart done at 10:48 UTC. Logs now show `Assertion validated` and users confirm SSO success. Customer also republished metadata with only the new cert at 10:49 UTC. Marking resolved for now; recommending eng follow-up to make metadata parsing tolerant of duplicate KeyDescriptor ordering and to normalize ACS/entityID canonicalization (trailing slash). Thanks everyone! :tada:
